title: Test Categories and Coverage
learning_outcomes: Explain the purpose of test categories and coverage in a FastAPI application.
Apply or interpret one example related to unit tests.
Identify one limitation or failure case and describe how to verify it.

content.intro: This lesson covers test categories and coverage within testing and code quality. Use the supplied syllabus topics as the coverage checklist, then connect them to the worked example and the verification task.
content.why_it_matters: You will use test categories and coverage to build APIs whose contracts and behavior are understandable to both clients and maintainers. The practical aim is repeatable checks, explicit expected outcomes, negative cases and actionable diagnostics.

content_blocks.title: Core idea
content_blocks.text: Test Categories and Coverage matters because it is part of testing and code quality. In practice, focus on repeatable checks, explicit expected outcomes, negative cases and actionable diagnostics. A framework feature only helps when its assumptions match the application; keep input validation, business policy and side effects distinguishable.

items.title: Unit tests
items.text: Use unit tests to make behavior observable and repeatable. Specify one normal case, one invalid or missing-input case, and the expected status or diagnostic. A passing happy path alone is not enough evidence.

content_blocks.title: Worked example: Test Categories and Coverage
content_blocks.expected_output: pytest reports one passing test when saved as a test file and pytest is installed.
content_blocks.run_instructions: Run pytest -q from the project environment; include failure and authorization cases as endpoints are added.
content_blocks.reset_steps: For read-only examples, no reset is needed. For any example that writes state, use a disposable local database/test fixture; record the starting state and clean up only lab data. Never use production credentials or real personal data.
content_blocks.limitations: This code is inspectable lesson material, not executed by CodeLeaf. Run it only in a local virtual environment or a separately isolated runner with resource/time/network limits. Security examples are sketches, not complete production authentication or authorization systems.

content_blocks.title: Try it yourself
content_blocks.text: Adapt the example to cover “Unit tests”. Write down the expected success result and one invalid, missing, duplicate, timeout or permission-boundary case that matters for this topic.

task: Create a small reviewable artifact for “Test Categories and Coverage”: explain its goal, cover the listed subtopics, show an example with expected result, then include one edge case and how you would verify it.
hints: Start with “Unit tests” and state the required inputs, output and assumptions.
Change one thing at a time; check the official reference and capture the actual response/error instead of guessing.
Include a negative/edge-case check and document which behavior remains untested.
expected_output: A reviewable example or design note for Test Categories and Coverage, covering the PDF subtopics, expected behavior and at least one verification check.

common_mistakes.problem: Copying a code fragment without checking its assumptions.
common_mistakes.why: Installed versions, imported types, application structure and external services affect behavior.
common_mistakes.fix: State assumptions; check the versioned official docs; run a minimal local test and add one failure case.

common_mistakes.problem: Treating one happy-path response as proof of correctness.
common_mistakes.why: Invalid input, permissions, concurrency, timeouts and cleanup are not exercised by a single request.
common_mistakes.fix: Add focused normal and negative tests and record exact expected status/body.

common_mistakes.why: Even short examples may mutate records, reveal data or affect availability.
common_mistakes.fix: Use synthetic inputs and a disposable environment; review security, cleanup and rollback before promotion.

summary: Test Categories and Coverage belongs to the broader goal of repeatable checks, explicit expected outcomes, negative cases and actionable diagnostics.
Use the source subtopics as the completeness checklist and verify expected results rather than relying on intuition.
Examples in this course are illustrative until technically reviewed and executed on a supported local environment.
